newsitem.title: UK: Rainfall improves Europe sugar beet prospects-Lich.
newsitem.headline: Rainfall improves Europe sugar beet prospects-Lich.

text.p: Adequate rainfall and moderate temperatures have improved crop prospects across most of Europe's sugar beet growing areas, German statistician F.O. Licht said on Wednesday.
In its daily report, Licht said weather conditions had again been excellent for beet growth during the week ended June 24.

It noted that parts of eastern Germany were still drier than normal although moisture levels were adequate for vegetative growth. Moisture in Italy was below normal but recent rains had improved crop prospects, it said.
Licht said rainfall had been light in Spain but crop conditions were stable as moisture levels were adequate.
Weather conditions for beet crops in eastern Europe were also favourable.
"Conditions in Eastern Europe are equally favourable apart from a few dry patches in Poland. Hungary, Romania and Bulgaria expect above average crops," Licht said.
But while growing areas in the former Soviet Union had received adequate rainfall to support further growth, adverse weather in Russia had also destroyed part of this year's area sown to beet.
This indicated that the Russian industry's beet production target of 22 million tonnes, after 14.77 million last year, was now out of reach, Licht said.
